chose: A point answered by a take of its own is `tickets[i].points[j].answer`: a take carries its transcript, one `mark` ({mark, note?}, the same shape as a whole take's `marks[i]`) and its own SOLO level; or a silence (a guess, or unheard). No `verdict` field yet: each point object is strict, so RR29's optional `verdict` is an additive field in a later version. Point answers are drawn from version 3 of the essay's template (ESSAY_POINT_VERSION): v3 allows 16 answer scenes (4 tickets, each its whole answer and up to 3 points), and the routine pins 3 only when a ticket has a point answered on its own. A v1 or v2 essay, and a v3 essay of whole takes, render exactly as before.
options: shape: `marks` of length one, sharing the whole take's schema
shape: a separate per-point list beside `points`
version: no version: an older stage refuses the unknown key anyway
gray: The server reads only `points[j].answer.kind`; how the reading inside is shaped is the essay's. A one-item `marks` would read the same on screen but invite a length check that means nothing. Either refuses an essay an older stage can't draw; the version says why in the owner's terms ("publish a newer stage first") and keeps the pinned formats honest about the answer scene's repeat count.
undo: Rename `mark` to `marks` in PointAnswerSchema and values.ts's PointValuesSchema; essays already written would need a new template version. Fold the change into version 2's format; essays written at 3 would then need re-pinning.
